choices.text: Curly arrows point from the electron-poor atom toward the electron-rich one.
Curly arrows start at an electron-rich region, such as a lone pair or a pi bond, and point to where the electrons go
Curly arrows show which atom slides across to form the new bond

questions.feedback: That trap reading is the one to unlearn: Curly arrows point from the electron-poor atom toward the electron-rich one. Reteach point: Curly arrows follow the electrons: they start at an electron-rich region (a lone pair or pi bond) and point to where the electrons go.
questions.misconception: Curly arrows point from the electron-poor atom toward the electron-rich one.
questions.prompt: Which statement about curly arrows is correct?

questions.answer: Hydroxide attacks opposite the C-Br bond so its lone pair can form the new C-O bond as the C-Br pair leaves with bromine, through a single transition state. The rate equation, rate = k[CH3Br][OH-], includes both reactants, which shows both meet in the one slow step.
questions.feedback: This is the concerted step of scene s5: one step, backside attack, and both reactants in the rate equation - the mirror image of SN1.
questions.prompt: In the SN2 reaction of CH3Br with OH-, why must the hydroxide attack from the back, and what does the rate equation tell you about the step?

choices.text: Ethanol, by nucleophilic substitution: OH- replaces Br on the carbon

questions.feedback: Hydroxide is a nucleophile and bromine is the leaving group (scene s6, step B of the route): Br is substituted by OH to give ethanol, CH3CH2OH.
questions.prompt: Bromoethane is warmed with aqueous sodium hydroxide. What is the product and the reaction type?

questions.answer: Atoms do not slide along curly arrows. The arrow tracks one pair of electrons: the H-Br bond pair moves onto bromine, which leaves as Br-, while the pi pair forms the new C-H bond.
questions.feedback: This is the trap scene s7: atoms stay put and only electron pairs move - the pair starts at the bond and ends on bromine.
questions.prompt: A student writes that in the ethene and HBr mechanism, the bromine atom slides along the curly arrow onto the carbon. Correct the student's reading in one or two sentences.
